triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるBundibugyoエボラウイルス株による史上最大規模の流行を報じている。シエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニアは2014-2016年西アフリカ流行との比較対象として言及されているのみで、現行イベントの発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebolagevallen in Democratische Republiek Congo boven de 10.000 na aanval waarbij verpleegster omkomt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 10,000 after an attack in which a nurse was killed.
article.articleSummary: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 10,000, with the death toll at 4,887 as of 25 October, and 40 of the latest 46 deaths occurring in the community rather than in treatment centers, signaling ongoing gaps in early detection and patient transfer. New infections have been reported in Ituri, North Kivu, and Tshopo provinces amid the largest outbreak on record in the country, now spreading beyond borders. Misinformation has spurred deadly violence against health workers, including an attack in Bafwasende on 24 October where a nurse was killed and a school principal severely wounded. A clinical trial for a Bundibugyo-strain Ebola vaccine has begun in Congo, with the first participant receiving Merck's Ervebo (protects against a different Ebola strain); Moderna and Oxford/Serum Institute vaccines are expected in the coming weeks. Emphasis remains on enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, safe burials, and protection of responders.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者が1万人を超える、看護師が死亡した襲撃事件を受けて
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が国境を越えて拡大し、死者数が多く、医療従事者への暴力も発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事は過去最大規模のエボラ流行の継続拡大、医療従事者への暴力、ワクチン臨床試験開始など複数の重要情報を含む。国境を越えた拡大が明記されており、周辺国への影響評価も必要。

article.articleHeadline: الإصابات بفيروس إيبولا في الكونغو تتجاوز 10 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Congo exceed 10,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-27, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reports 10,060 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, up from 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths reported on Oct 13. Ebola is a highly contagious hemorrhagic fever transmitted through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people. The DRC has a long history of Ebola outbreaks, with repeated waves posing ongoing health and economic challenges for the country and the region. The report centers on confirmed case counts and does not detail infection sources, laboratory methods, or any imported/exported cases. The information reflects a protracted outbreak within a nation historically prone to Ebola transmission, underscoring persistent public health concerns in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱感染者数が1万人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱確定例が10,060例、死亡4,381例に達し、致死率も高く深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 致死率は約43.5%と非常に高く、長期化する流行であり、国際的な支援と監視が必要と考えられる。感染源や検査方法の詳細は記事に記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases as authorities race to slow the spread in African countries - The Korea Times
article.articleSummary: Congolese Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus has reached 10,060 confirmed cases with nearly 5,000 deaths, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing outbreak in Congo's history. Declared in May, it has spread across 66 health zones in eight provinces and reached three regions, with cases also in Kenya and Nigeria; Uganda and France are among five affected countries but have no active cases currently. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo virus. About 2,600 patients have recovered. Challenges include armed conflict, poor roads, mistrust, and violence toward responders, plus health worker strikes over unpaid wages. About 80% of new cases come from outside monitored contacts; maternal mortality has doubled in some provinces as pregnant women avoid hospitals. A virtual Africa CDC summit is planned to bolster cross-border response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが1万人を突破、アフリカ諸国で当局が感染拡大阻止を急ぐ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）アウトブレイクが1万例・死者約5000人に達し、コンゴ史上最も致死的かつ急拡大している疫病であり、複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアでも症例が報告され、ウガンダ・フランスは過去に症例があったが現在は活動性症例なしとされる。これら4カ国は対象国リスト外または主題国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しない点、武装紛争・医療従事者ストライキ等の対応阻害要因が深刻性を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: '에볼라 공포'...민주콩고서 확진자 1만명 넘고, 사망자 4887명 달해
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'Ebola Fear'... In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, confirmed cases exceed 10,000, and deaths reach 4,887.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths (case fatality 48.6%) as of Oct 25, 2026, 165 days after outbreak declaration. The outbreak began May 15 in Ituri and has spread through North Kivu and South Kivu to a northwestern Ubangi region, affecting eight provinces across 66 health zones. The circulating virus is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no approved vaccine or therapy exists. The outbreak’s pace is faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, with more than 4,000 deaths within six months. Contributing factors include security instability, distrust of healthcare workers, and lack of effective countermeasures. Cross-border concerns include Uganda reporting 20 cases (including 15 imports) with 2 deaths; Kenya and Nigeria also reported cases linked to travel from the region, including a Kenyan national who returned via Uganda and a Nigerian spouse of a Swiss diplomat who had visited Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: 『エボラの恐怖』…コンゴ民主共和国で確診者1万人超、死者4887人に達する
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模なエボラアウトブレイク（1万人超の症例、致死率48.6%）が発生し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境拡大が確認されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。承認されたワクチン・治療法が存在しないBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行で、致死率48.6%と極めて高く、2014-2016年西アフリカ流行より拡大速度が速い点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Una ciudadana suiza con ébola fue trasladada desde Nigeria a Ginebra junto a su esposo diplomático
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A Swiss citizen with Ebola was transported from Nigeria to Geneva with her diplomat husband.
article.articleSummary: Swiss citizen, 42, born in Uganda, diagnosed with Ebola in Abuja, Nigeria, was evacuated to Switzerland with her diplomat husband. The medical airlift occurred Monday under strict biosecurity with Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad Pate’s authorization. The patient is stable, conscious, and able to communicate, but may remain contagious; precautions remain in place. She receives treatment at the University Hospital of Geneva in quarantine, while her husband is isolated at the University Hospital of Zurich as a preventive measure. Switzerland’s Federal Office of Public Health asserts both hospitals are prepared for Ebola care. Nigeria reports 52 exposed individuals as it sustains containment; no active cases, marking Nigeria's first in over a decade. The woman developed symptoms four days after returning to Abuja following about 2.5 weeks in Uganda. Nigeria’s NCDC is sequencing the virus, confirming Bundibugyo Ebola virus; exposure may trace to Uganda rather than the Congo, with Entebbe transit noted.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱に感染したスイス人女性が、外交官の夫とともにナイジェリアからジュネーブへ搬送された
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアで10年以上ぶりとなるエボラ出血熱症例が確認され、患者が国際的に（スイスへ）搬送されたことで国境を越えた感染拡大リスクがあり、52名の濃厚接触者が確認されているため。
triage.notes: 感染確認・発症はナイジェリア（アブジャ）、感染経路はウガンダ滞在歴に関連する可能性が高いとされ、コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）は明示的に除外されている。患者はスイスへ空輸され隔離治療中。いずれも対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Fears Mount as Diplomat's Wife Is Evacuated to Switzerland and Nigeria Monitors 52 Contacts
article.articleSummary: As of 27 October 2026, Ebola fears mount as a Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat in Abuja, infected with the Bundibugyo strain, was evacuated from Nigeria to Switzerland on 26 October and hospitalised in Geneva; her husband is in isolation at Zurich University Hospital. The patient is described as stable, conscious and 'closing towards baseline' in lab results, though officials caution she may still be infectious. Nigeria monitors 52 people who may have been exposed; 53 were identified initially. Switzerland will oversee treatment; Nigeria remains responsible for monitoring other contacts. The case marks Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola infection in over a decade; investigators are probing transmission routes, including a possible link to Entebbe Airport. Uganda had previously declared Ebola-free, while Kenya has nine cases and two deaths. The Congo Bundibugyo outbreak has caused the vast majority of infections (over 9,900) and 4,800 deaths since May.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ懸念拡大：外交官の妻がスイスへ搬送、ナイジェリアは52人の接触者を監視
triage.triage_reason: DRCで継続するブンディブギョ株アウトブレイク（感染9900人超、死亡4800人）が、ナイジェリアでの10年ぶりの確定例やスイスへの国際搬送という形で国際的拡大を見せており、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高いためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主たる発生源はDRCにおける大規模ブンディブギョ株アウトブレイク（9900人感染、4800人死亡）。ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・スイスは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCでの継続的流行状況が国際的波及の根本原因であるため、フルRRAによる詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: EXCLUSIVE: Co-Diagnostics Moves Closer to Commercial Tuberculosis Test Launch in India - Co-Diagnostics (
article.articleSummary: Co-Diagnostics' India joint venture, CoSara Diagnostics Pvt. Ltd., filed with India's CDSCO for clearance of the CoSara PCR Mycobacterium tuberculosis test on the CoSara PCR Pro, moving toward a South Asia launch. A multicenter clinical evaluation across Indian laboratories enrolled 676 patient samples, including 233 MGIT-paired specimens, yielding 97.3% sensitivity and 96.0% specificity against a tuberculosis reference standard, with consistent performance across test lots. The portable CoSara PCR Pro uses proprietary Co-Primers to deliver real-time TB PCR results in about 30 minutes via a mobile app, enabling decentralized testing without constant internet; an India-local cloud and mobile architecture supports data synchronization when connectivity resumes. India accounts for roughly a quarter of global TB infections per WHO Global TB Report 2025, underscoring market importance. Regulatory authorization is anticipated in Q4 2026, with a commercial rollout in India before year end.

triage.headline_ja: 独占：Co-Diagnostics社、インドでの結核検査商業化に向け前進
triage.triage_reason: これは結核診断検査の規制承認・商業展開に関するビジネス記事であり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は結核診断製品の規制申請・臨床性能に関する企業ニュースであり、感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではないため対象国に含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Segundo foco da doença de Newcastle coloca agro em alerta; ouça o comentário
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Second outbreak of Newcastle disease puts agriculture on alert; listen to the commentary.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-27, a second Newcastle disease focus has been confirmed in western Santa Catarina, Brazil, at a turkey-breeding nucleus in Coronel Freitas, about 35 kilometers from Nova Itaberaba, where the virus was first detected. In addition to outbreaks on commercial farms, the pathogen has been identified in free-living pigeons in Marema, outside the zoosanitary emergency area. The report underscores the geographic expansion of the Newcastle disease situation in the region and highlights the need for continued surveillance and biosecurity in affected farms and nearby wild-bird populations. No mortality or laboratory confirmation details are provided in the brief for authorities.

triage.headline_ja: ニューカッスル病の2例目の発生、農業に警戒態勢をもたらす；解説を聴く
triage.triage_reason: 動物疾患（ニューカッスル病）のブラジル国内拡大事例であり、養鶏産業への影響と野生鳥類への拡散が懸念されるが、ヒトへの健康影響情報はなく、続報を注視する段階。
triage.notes: 動物（七面鳥・野生ハト）における家禽疾患であり、ヒト感染リスクは記事に記載なし。貿易・農業への影響が主眼。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية تبدأ تجربة سريرية للقاحات إيبولا بونديبوجيو في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization begins a clinical trial of Bundibugyo Ebola vaccines in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization has launched a Phase I clinical trial of Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccines in the Democratic Republic of Congo, following vaccination of four participants in the first phase in Bunia. The brief confirms vaccine testing against this Ebola species but provides limited details. Four individuals in Bunia reportedly received the investigational vaccine as part of the initial cohort; no safety outcomes, immunogenicity data, case counts, fatalities, or transmission information are disclosed. Bundibugyo ebolavirus is one of the Ebola viruses, and the article highlights ongoing efforts to develop vaccines that cover multiple Ebola lineages. No further information on trial design, endpoints, recruitment, or regulatory status is included in the report.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関、コンゴでブンディブギョ・エボラワクチンの臨床試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は実際のエボラ発生・感染拡大ではなく、WHOによるワクチン臨床試験（第I相、参加者4名）の開始を報じるものであり、症例数・死亡者・感染拡大等の公衆衛生上の懸念情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事は進行中のアウトブレイクではなく、ブンディブギョ種エボラウイルスに対する予防的ワクチン臨床試験（第I相）の開始を報じたもの。実際の感染症例・死亡・伝播状況の記載はなく、研究開発ニュースとして位置づけられる。

article.articleHeadline: Caso da doença de Newcastle em Santa Catarina coloca setor avícola gaúcho em alerta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Case of Newcastle disease in Santa Catarina puts Rio Grande do Sul's poultry sector on alert.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 October 2026, Newcastle disease has triggered a zoosanitary emergency in four Santa Catarina municipalities—Nova Itaberaba, Águas Frias, Coronel Freitas, and Nova Erechim—after the virus was detected at a poultry facility in Nova Itaberaba. A Diário Oficial da União portaria imposes a 60-day restriction on exports of Santa Catarina chicken meat. Rio Grande do Sul remains on alert to prevent entry and spread, with Agriculture Secretary Márcio Madalena highlighting enhanced sanitary surveillance in coordination with the federal Ministry of Agriculture. The last Newcastle case in Rio Grande do Sul was July 2024 in Anta Gorda (Vale do Taquari); no new notifications since. Producers should monitor flocks and report suspected cases promptly. Newcastle disease is highly contagious among birds; human infection is rare, usually conjunctivitis in exposed individuals. Mexico suspended Brazilian chicken meat and other poultry imports to protect its disease-free production, impacting exports and sector confidence.

triage.headline_ja: サンタカタリーナ州でのニューカッスル病発生により、リオグランデ・ド・スル州の養鶏業界が警戒態勢
triage.triage_reason: 家禽向けニューカッスル病の発生で輸出制限やメキシコの輸入停止など貿易面への影響が出ているが、人への感染リスクは低く（まれに結膜炎程度）、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響は確認されていないため、動向を注視する段階と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Thanh Hóa khẩn trương khoanh vùng dập dịch tả lợn châu Phi ở Tân Thành
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Thanh Hoa Province urgently cordons off and contains the African swine fever outbreak in Tan Thanh.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever outbreak in Tan Thanh commune, Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam. From Oct 9, 2026, pigs in Thanh Nang hamlet began showing illness and deaths; laboratory testing confirmed ASF virus. By Oct 21, two additional outbreaks emerged in Thanh Lam and Luân Khe hamlets. By Oct 26, 2026, 46 pigs across 3 of 7 hamlets were infected or culled, weighing over 2.1 tonnes. On Oct 27, authorities ordered immediate cordon-off, culling of all infected and dead pigs under biosafety protocols, disinfection and sanitation, enhanced surveillance, and strict controls on movement, sale, and slaughter of pigs to prevent spread. The aim is containment in Tan Thanh by Nov 30, 2026. Across Thanh Hoa, as of Oct 26, 2026, 14 communes remain under ASF surveillance beyond 21 days, with 4,094 pigs culled (286.799 tonnes) across 318 households; two inspection teams are guiding 16 border communes and gates.

triage.headline_ja: タインホア省タンタイン地区でアフリカ豚熱(ASF)流行、緊急封じ込めを実施
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱は豚のみに感染し人への感染性（ズーノーシス性）がないため、公衆衛生上の脅威とはならず、国際的な人の健康リスクも認められない。
triage.notes: ASFは家畜(豚)のみの感染症であり、ヒトへの感染リスクはないため対象国リストへの計上は行わない。農業・畜産分野の管理事案として地元当局が対応中。

article.articleHeadline: Над 10 000 са потвърдените случаи на ебола в Конго, 50% от заболелите са починали -- OFFNews
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases in Congo, 50% of those infected have died -- OFFNews.
article.articleSummary: Over 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with about 5,030 deaths (roughly 50% mortality) according to government data released today, as health authorities push to curb the outbreak spreading across several African countries. The outbreak, declared in May, is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Approximately 10,060 cases have been reported; half have died, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. Response efforts face major obstacles, including armed conflict, poor road infrastructure, and violence fueled by mistrust and misinformation, complicating case reporting and care-seeking. By comparison, the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak had over 28,000 cases and more than 11,000 deaths; in the current outbreak, reported infections and deaths are at least three times higher for the same period since onset. Monitor for updates.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ確認症例が1万人を超える、致死率50%
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の症例が1万人を超え、致死率約50%と歴史的最大規模の流行であり、IHR基準複数該当・社会的関心も高いためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 記事はアンゴラにも言及しているが対象国リストに含まれず、主題はコンゴ民主共和国での流行。ワクチン・治療法未承認、武力紛争やインフラ未整備が対応を困難にしていると記載。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果民主伊波拉确诊破万例 防疫宣导人员遇袭身亡 - 国际 - 即时国际
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo surpasses 10,000 confirmed cases; public health outreach workers attacked and killed - International - Live International
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, with 10,060 cases and an estimated 48.6% fatality rate reported as of Oct 23, 2026. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain is circulating across eight provinces, including Tshopo Province. Health authorities reported that two public health outreach workers were attacked after locals accused them of polluting water sources while they were assessing land; a nurse from Bafwasende town General Hospital was killed on the spot, and a teacher colleague was injured but survived. The attacks illustrate severe trust gaps hindering outbreak control, with threats extending to hospitals, vehicles, and staff involved in Ebola prevention efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、確認症例1万例を突破 防疫啓発活動員が襲撃され死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が8州に拡大し致死率約48.6%と深刻で、コミュニティの不信による医療従事者襲撃も発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 致死率約48.6%、8州に拡大、医療従事者への暴力的攻撃が発生しており、アウトブレイク対応への信頼低下が懸念される。フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de ebola se extinde în RD Congo: peste 10.000 de cazuri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is spreading in DR Congo: over 10,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports 10,060 confirmed Ebola infections and 4,887 deaths from the Bundibugyo strain as of October 27, 2026, per the National Public Health Institute. The outbreak extends across 66 health zones in eight provinces, with control hampered by insecurity, poor transport infrastructure, limited healthcare access, and community distrust. Many new cases occur outside monitored contact networks, complicating transmission tracing. The outbreak has reached neighboring countries: Kenya has nine cases (one death) among people who contacted the initial patient, while Nigeria has confirmed an imported case in Abuja, under isolation and investigation. There is no licensed vaccine or proven targeted treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola; supportive care remains essential. A Bundibugyo vaccine candidate began a clinical trial in RD Congo on Oct 23, with initial participants enrolled in Bunia. WHO advises against travel restrictions but calls for strengthened regional surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行がコンゴ民主共和国で拡大：症例数1万人超
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がDRC国内8州66保健地区に拡大し、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際的拡散も確認されているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大が報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。治安不安、医療アクセス不足、接触者追跡の困難さが制御を妨げている。ワクチン未承認で臨床試験が開始されたばかり。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola cases top 10,000 as outbreak tests Africa's defenses
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak surpasses 10,000 cases: 10,060 confirmed, 4,887 deaths (case fatality 48.6%) as of Oct 25. Ituri remains epicenter, >70% of cases, with eight of 26 provinces and 66 health zones affected. Ongoing transmission amid conflict and displacement strains surveillance; early detection and contact tracing are weak, with only about 12% of confirmed cases linked to known contacts. Cross-border spread linked to Uganda, France, Kenya and Nigeria since May. Kenya reports nine confirmed cases (two deaths) and 98 contacts under monitoring; the first imported Kenyan national who lived in DRC died Oct 5. Nigeria’s index patient traveled from Uganda; confirmed Oct 20; 52 contacts under monitoring; Nigeria has no current confirmed cases, source unclear; joint Uganda-Nigeria investigation. Uganda remains Ebola-free, but has tightened measures. Vaccines race: Tumaini Phase 2/3 in Bunia; Ervebo candidate and Bundibugyo-specific candidates from Moderna and Oxford/Serum Institute of India being considered.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ症例が1万人を突破、アウトブレイクはアフリカの防疫体制を試す
triage.triage_reason: 症例数1万人超・致死率48.6%という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトに加え、複数国（ケニア、ナイジェリア）への越境拡大が確認されており、IHR基準の複数項目に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・フランスへの越境関連症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。主たる発生地はDRC（特にIturi州）。接触者追跡率が低く（約12%）、紛争・避難民により監視体制が脆弱な点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: To Contribute to the World, Prabowo Urges Acceleration of Malaria Vaccine Research
article.articleSummary: On 27 October 2026, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto urged BRIN head Arif Satria to accelerate malaria vaccine research, aiming for completion within three years. He emphasized support for production and noted there is currently no vaccine for malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax, suggesting Indonesia could contribute to global health if the BRIN-led effort succeeds. BRIN is pursuing malaria vaccines with four candidates, with Indonesia hosting roughly five to six candidates in total, developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Bio Farma. Prabowo’s attention to vaccine independence is evident, with frequent inquiries into progress. Beyond vaccines, he backs drug independence via herbal medicines; BRIN has 19 herbal candidates under consideration for fitofarmaka, transitioning from OHT to clinical trials in coordination with the Ministry of Health and BPOM.

triage.headline_ja: 世界への貢献のため、プラボウォ大統領がマラリアワクチン研究の加速を要請
triage.triage_reason: 政策・研究開発に関する発表であり、具体的な感染拡大や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報がないため、シグナルとしては該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事はマラリアワクチン研究加速に関する政府の方針発表であり、実際の感染症発生・流行に関する情報ではないため、対象国の発生国としては計上しない。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 10,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reached 10,060 confirmed cases with 4,887 deaths, according to the DRC Public Health Institute. The outbreak, declared in mid-May 2026, is the largest and most deadly Ebola outbreak in the country’s history, surpassing the 2018–2020 period. Health authorities warn that transmission could widen, raising concerns about spread to other African countries. The numbers reflect ongoing transmission since the May declaration, based on laboratory-confirmed cases reported by national surveillance. The report underscores the severity and scale of the outbreak and the need for continued vigilance and regional cooperation to contain spread and prevent cross-border transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Κονγκό: Όχλος οπλισμένος με ματσέτες σκότωσε νοσοκόμα που φρόντιζε ασθενείς με Έμπολα
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: An armed mob with machetes killed a nurse who cared for Ebola patients.
article.articleSummary: An armed mob killed a nurse who aided Ebola patients in Congo, injuring another health worker, in the latest violence fueled by misinformation about the deadly virus. The attackers, armed with knives and clubs, targeted the pair and accused them of spreading the disease by contaminating water sources. The nurse was based at the General Hospital in Bafwasende, where she helped raise awareness about the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, which the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Health says has killed more than 4,800 people since the outbreak began in May. The World Health Organization condemned the attack; Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus emphasized that health workers must be able to work with dignity and safety. Security measures are in place, with police protection at the hospital and brief army deployment in the region.

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يتجاوز 10 آلاف إصابة في الكونغو الديمقراطية ومخاوف من تمدده أفريقياً
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 10,000 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with fears of its spread across Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, reaching 10,060 with 4,887 deaths, according to government data as of 2026-10-27. The outbreak, attributed to the rare Bundibugyo strain, began in mid-May and is the largest and deadliest on record in the DRC. It ranks as the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, which killed more than 11,000 people in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Imported spread has reached other countries: Kenya reported its first case this month, bringing nine total infections after a Nairobi man who traveled from Congo via Uganda died; Nigeria also confirmed a fourth African case. Uganda had about 20 cases in May–June, mostly imported; WHO later declared Uganda free in August, though authorities say no domestic transmission now. Uganda enforces a 21-day quarantine for returnees from Congo.

article.articleHeadline: Ебола се разпространява из Африка: случаите в Конго вече са над 10 000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is spreading across Africa: cases in Congo are already over 10,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, with 10,060 infections and about half deaths. Originating in May, it is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no licensed vaccines or treatments exist. The outbreak is the fastest-growing and deadliest on record in DRC. Transmission chains remain unclear, with about 80% of new cases not linked to known contacts; control requires at least 95% of new cases from known contacts. By October 2026 it has spread to eight provinces across 66 health zones, straining facilities, triggering strikes in Ituri's Nia Nia zone, and amid attacks on health workers including a nurse killed in Chopo. Five countries have reported imported cases: Kenya (nine cases, two deaths) and Nigeria, with Uganda and France also reporting infections but no active transmission. The crisis diverts resources from cholera and routine care, worsening maternal, immunization, and other health services.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in DR Congo surpass 10,000 in fastest-growing outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of 27 October 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths, the fastest-growing and deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or treatment, though a first vaccine clinical trial has rolled out. Declared 15 May, cases have spread to 66 health zones across eight provinces, with about 80% of new infections arising outside known transmission chains. The wider outbreak is the second-largest and second-deadliest globally, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Health systems are strained—overwhelmed treatment centers, shortages, and wage-related strikes; roughly half of fatalities were not admitted for treatment. Cross-border spread is evident: Uganda requires a 21-day quarantine for returnees; 20 Ugandan cases and 2 deaths; a Swiss patient linked to Uganda and Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland; Kenya reports 9 cases, 2 deaths, with 98 contacts under monitoring.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者が1万人を突破、史上最速の拡大を見せる流行に

article.articleHeadline: Ebola scientists to probe Nigeria case origin, Africa CDC says
article.articleSummary: The Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has nearly 10,000 cases and more than 4,600 deaths, spreading to Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda—the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya said a team of leading Ebola scientists will travel to Nigeria to investigate how the country’s first patient in more than a decade, Ugandan-born wife in Abuja, contracted the virus; travel documents show she had not visited the Congo epicenter. Genomic sequencing shows the Nigerian case and a Kenya case earlier this month were closely related, prompting examination of a possible link; Kenya’s patient, who died, was in the airport around the time, with flights about 40 minutes apart and no confirmed contact. The Nigerian patient had been in Uganda and travelled through Entebbe on Oct 3. Ebola Bundibugyo spreads through close contact with infected bodily fluids. Investigators aim to trace contacts and prevent silent spread.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の科学者ら、ナイジェリア症例の感染経路を調査へ―アフリカCDC発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ・ブンディブギョ流行は約1万症例・4600人超の死者を出し史上2番目の規模で、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへ国際的に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニアでも症例が確認されているが、これらは評価対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。アウトブレイクの震源地であるDRCのみを記載。

article.articleHeadline: Initiative to combat disease outbreaks in Africa launched
article.articleSummary: Africa CDC launches the Africa Research Preparedness Programme in West Africa to strengthen research governance, evidence generation, clinical trial readiness and regional coordination for rapid outbreak response and global health security. The programme aims to establish clinical trial sites even in non-outbreak periods to coordinate regional responses when crises occur. West Africa is the first regional pilot, with hubs in Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR, Ghana), MRC Unit The Gambia, Burkina Faso and Nigeria for sub-regional trials; success could guide expansion to East and Central Africa. West Africa’s outbreak history includes Ebola, Lassa Fever and Monkeypox, among other pathologies. Attendees included WAHO, African Medicines Agency, WHO AFRO, NMIMR Director Prof. Dorothy Yeboah Manu, Africa CDC leadership Prof. Placide Kingebeni Mbala, WAHO, and CEPI representatives. Dr. Aishat Bukola Usman notes WAHO has awarded about $505 million in research grants to West African institutions since 2023.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカの感染症アウトブレイク対策のための新構想が始動
triage.triage_reason: 特定の感染症アウトブレイク発生を報じるものではなく、研究準備体制強化プログラムの立ち上げに関する報道であり、トリアージ対象となる具体的な公衆衛生事象ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はAfrica CDCによる研究準備プログラム（Africa Research Preparedness Programme）の西アフリカでの立ち上げを報じるもので、現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイクを報じるものではない。過去の流行歴（エボラ、ラッサ熱、サル痘）への言及はあるが、現時点での発生事例ではないためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Vigilância é ampliada em Coronel Freitas após novo foco da Doença de Newcastle - BelosF7
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Surveillance is being expanded in Coronel Freitas after a new Newcastle disease outbreak - BelosF7
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease outbreak in Western Santa Catarina, Brazil, triggers expanded surveillance after a second focus is identified at a commercial turkey farm in Coronel Freitas, housing 36,800 birds. Surveillance radius expanded 2.5 kilometers northeast of the initial area, incorporating 145 properties, including eight commercial establishments. In Nova Itaberaba, cleaning and disinfection is complete and the property is in sanitary empty status. Integrated efforts coordinated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Mapa) and the Santa Catarina Agricultural Defense Company (Cidasc) have established an Animal Health Emergency Operations Center in Oeste Catarinense, with involvement from regional and federal agencies. Producers are being educated on biosafety and clinical signs, and are urged to report suspected cases to the local Cidasc office or via e-Sisbravet. Municipalities currently under sanitary emergency status remain Nova Itaberaba, Nova Erechim, Coronel Freitas, and Águas Frias.

triage.headline_ja: ニューカッスル病の新たな発生拠点確認を受け、コロネル・フレイタスで監視体制を強化―BelosF7
triage.triage_reason: 家きんにおける動物疾病（ニューカッスル病）の発生であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生影響は報告されていないが、商業養鶏産業への影響と拡大監視体制から動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 本事案は動物（家きん）の感染症であり、ヒトへの感染症例は報告されていない。公衆衛生上の直接的リスクは低いが、家禽産業・貿易への影響の可能性があるため経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo surpass 10,000 as deaths mount
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 10,060 cases this week, according to the DRC Health Ministry, marking the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. The epidemic has killed about 4,800 people since it began in May. The surge underscores escalating transmission and heightens concerns that the outbreak could cross borders and spread to other African nations. Nigeria, Kenya, and Uganda have each reported several Ebola cases this year, illustrating regional transmission risk. Health authorities face ongoing challenges in containment, surveillance, and response as case counts rise. The article notes the rapid expansion within the DRC and the potential for cross-border spread among neighboring countries, emphasizing the need for coordinated public health measures to prevent further importations.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、症例数が1万人を超え死者も増加
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱が史上最速ペースで拡大し、1万例・死者4,800人に達しており、周辺国（ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダ）への越境拡大リスクも報告されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、越境拡大リスクとしてRRAで考慮すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Regional body backs intensified Ebola screening at four Kenyan entry points
article.articleSummary: ECSA-HC backs intensified Ebola screening at four Kenyan entry points after imported Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease case and infections among contacts. Launched Oct 22 in Nairobi, the seven-point preparedness package targets Jomo Kenyatta International Airport and Busia, Malaba, and Lwakhakha border points to strengthen screening, surveillance, emergency response and protection. Components include gap assessments, emergency simulations, harmonised screening and referral procedures, digital surveillance, 21-day traveller follow-up, infection prevention, and laboratory readiness. The move follows rising Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo in August; by Oct 22 nine entry points along borders had been reached under World Bank-funded Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Programme. Kenya emphasizes prevention to contain spread; port health officials intensified screening at airports, land borders and maritime points, with suspected cases isolated. Training for PPE, safe sample handling, and community informants are integrated into event-based surveillance. Partners include WHO, Africa CDC and IOM.

triage.headline_ja: 地域保健機関、ケニア国内4つの入国地点でのエボラ出血熱スクリーニング強化を支持
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ発生拡大を受け、ケニアへの輸入症例が確認されており、国際的拡大と渡航制限措置（入国時スクリーニング強化）が既に実施されているためIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCで8月以降増加しているエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の発生とそれに伴うケニアでの輸入症例・水際対策強化。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、発生源であるDRCのみを記載した。WHO、Africa CDC、IOM、世界銀行が関与しており国際的な懸念・支援体制が既に構築されている。

article.articleHeadline: إصابات "إيبولا" في الكونغو تتجاوز 10 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 10,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, with 4,887 deaths, according to a government report. The Public Health Institute said the tally reached 10,060 cases, marking the largest and deadliest outbreak in the DRC since the 2018–2020 epidemic. The mid-May wave is linked to the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. Earlier this month Kenya reported its first case and has since logged nine cases, after a Nairobi fatality of a man who had traveled from the Congo via Uganda. Last week Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola infection, underscoring rising regional transmission risk. The outbreak prompted international concern over potential spread to additional African nations.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ感染者数が1万人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱がIHR複数基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大）に該当し、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境伝播も確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大が報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。主たる発生国はDRC。

article.articleHeadline: Более 10 тыс. случаев заражения Эболой зарегистрировали в ДР Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 10,000 Ebola cases registered in DR Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo has registered over 10,000 Ebola cases, with the health ministry counting 10,060 infections and more than 5,000 deaths. The outbreak was officially declared on 15 May in Ituri province, and infections have been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. Earlier updates cited about 9,000 cases and 4,300 deaths. In late August, the World Health Organization announced that transmission in Uganda had ceased. Earlier reports noted the first Ebola death in Kenya. These figures reflect the evolving toll across the region, with Congo bearing the largest burden as of late October, according to authorities.

triage.headline_ja: DR コンゴで1万人超のエボラ感染例が登録
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRコンゴで1万人超・死者5000人超に達し、複数国（ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ）への越境拡大が報告されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク）に該当するため。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。ウガンダでは8月末にWHOが感染伝播終息を発表済み。致死率(約50%)が高い点にも留意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : plus de 10 000 cas d'Ebola confirmés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: More than 10,000 Confirmed Ebola Cases.
article.articleSummary: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak has crossed 10,000 confirmed cases, with the latest bulletin reporting 10,060 laboratory-confirmed infections. The announcement, from Kinshasa, was issued by the Public Health Institute of the DRC (Institut de santé publique) and cited by Reuters. The previous bulletin on the 13th of the month recorded 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths. Historically among the nations most exposed to Ebola, the DRC has experienced multiple flare-ups, posing substantial health and economic challenges for the country and the wider region. The report highlights ongoing transmission risk in the DRC and the need for continued public health response. Keywords: Ebola, Democratic Republic of Congo, outbreak, Kinshasa, 10,060 cases, 4,381 deaths (previous).

triage.headline_ja: DRC：エボラ確認症例が1万人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確認症例が10,000例を超え、致死率も高く、公衆衛生上深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 致死率は約43.5%（4,381/10,060、直近集計時点）と非常に高く、継続的な感染拡大リスクが示唆される。続報での感染拡大地域・対応状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Masisi : le choléra fait cinq morts en moins d'une semaine dans le groupement Ufamandu 1, alerte sur le manque de médicaments
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Masisi: Cholera has killed five people in less than a week in the Ufamandu 1 groupement, warning about medicine shortages.
article.articleSummary: Cholera and malaria are reported in Ufamandu 1 groupement, Masisi Territory, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with five cholera deaths in less than a week. The health crisis comes as cases have been rising for several days and local facilities are paralysed by medicine shortages, hindering timely treatment and increasing risk, especially for children under five. The return of some families to their home areas has not yet improved access to care. Medical sources urge urgent intervention by authorities and partners to replenish essential medicines and restore health services. Residents request targeted protection for young children against complications and swift resupply to prevent further fatalities while health systems resume functioning.

triage.headline_ja: マシシ：ウファマンドゥ1グループマンでコレラにより1週間未満で5人死亡、医薬品不足を警告
triage.triage_reason: コレラによる死亡例が急増し、医薬品不足により医療対応が機能不全となっているため、WPRO基準の複数項目に該当し、外部支援の必要性も示唆される。
triage.notes: DRC北キブ州は紛争や避難民の移動が続く地域であり、コレラの流行しやすい状況が継続している。医薬品不足による死亡増加が報告されており、現地当局・パートナーへの緊急介入要請がある。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo DR ar Ebolas vīrusu inficējušies jau vismaz 10 000 cilvēku - Medikamentu Informācijas Centrs
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In DR Congo, at least 10,000 people have been infected with the Ebola virus - Drug Information Center.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has infected at least 10,060 people with about 5,030 deaths, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. Launched in May 2026, the outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Experts say many infections remain undetected as the epidemic spread for months before detection. Healthcare workers face armed conflict, poor roads, distrust, and misinformation, with salary delays triggering strikes. The outbreak has expanded from 3 health zones in May to 66 zones across eight provinces. About 80% of cases are among people not on surveillance lists, indicating ongoing transmission chains. Cases have appeared in Kenya and Nigeria; five countries have reported infections, including Uganda and France, which currently have no active cases. As of 27 October 2026, the crisis strains health services and disrupts vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラウイルスに少なくとも1万人が感染
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模・最速拡大のエボラ流行（感染者10,060人、死亡5,030人）が発生し、複数国への拡大、ワクチン・治療法の欠如、保健システムの逼迫が確認されており、IHR基準を複数満たす重大事案。
triage.notes: 発生地域にケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランスが含まれるが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。致死率約50%と極めて高く、武装紛争や医療従事者ストライキなど対応能力にも深刻な課題がある。

article.articleHeadline: Λαϊκή Δημοκρατία του Κονγκό: Ξεπέρασαν τα 10.000 τα κρούσματα Έμπολα - Φόβοι για εξάπλωση της επιδημίας στην Αφρική
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Over 10,000 Ebola cases – Fears of the epidemic spreading in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases, with 4,887 deaths, as of Oct. 27, 2026, per the latest epidemiological bulletin (10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths). The outbreak, beginning in May and caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, has become the second-largest and deadliest on record, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone: ≈28,600 cases, ≈11,000 deaths). Cross-border concerns rose after Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case in October following a Nairobi death of a man who traveled from Congo via Uganda; Kenya now totals nine cases. Nigeria reported a fourth African country with Ebola. A Swiss diplomat’s wife infected in Nigeria is being traced to Uganda. Uganda imposes a 21-day quarantine for travelers returning from Congo, after earlier statements of no active cases, underscoring ongoing efforts to curb transmission across Africa.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ症例が1万人を超える ― アフリカでの流行拡大への懸念
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ症例数が1万人を超え致死率も高く、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダなど複数国への国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダでの症例も報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCが主要発生地かつ対象国リストに該当するため記載。

article.articleHeadline: Πάνω από 10.000 κρούσματα Έμπολα στο Κονγκό - Εντείνονται οι φόβοι ότι η επιδημία θα εξαπλωθεί και σε άλλες χώρες
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 10,000 Ebola cases in Congo - fears intensify that the outbreak will spread to other countries.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo faces an Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. As of the latest government report, 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths have been recorded. Initiated in mid-May, it is the largest and deadliest outbreak in the DRC, second only to the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (over 28,600 cases, >11,000 deaths). Kenya reported its first case earlier this month, with nine cases after a man died in Nairobi who had traveled from Congo via Uganda. Nigeria also reported a case, making it the fourth African country affected. Investigations into the Swiss diplomat’s wife who had not traveled to Congo point to Uganda as the exposure site; she and her husband were evacuated to Switzerland. Uganda had 20 May–June cases, was declared Ebola-free by WHO in August, and now requires 21-day quarantines for Congo returnees.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで1万人超のエボラ感染 - 他国への拡大懸念が強まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行（1万人超感染、死者約4,887人）が発生し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスへの国際的拡大が確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も極めて高い。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行を主題としている。ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスへの拡大が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα: Ξεπέρασαν τα 10.000 τα κρούσματα στο Κονγκό - Φόβοι για εξάπλωση της επιδημίας στην Αφρική
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Over 10,000 cases in the Congo - Fears of the epidemic spreading in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceed 10,000 cases, with 10,060 confirmed and 4,887 deaths, driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Initiated mid-May, the epidemic is the largest and most deadly Congo has faced, and ranks as the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally, after 2014–2016 West Africa. In early October, Kenya confirmed nine cases after a man who died in Nairobi had traveled from Congo via Uganda. Nigeria later reported its first case, the wife of a Swiss diplomat who had not visited Congo; authorities are investigating exposure, and Switzerland suspects Uganda as the infection source. Uganda previously recorded about 20 cases in May–June, mainly imported from Congo, and, despite WHO declaring Uganda Ebola-free in August, will quarantine returning Ugandan nationals from Congo for 21 days to curb importation.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴで症例が1万人を超える - アフリカでの流行拡大への懸念
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は1万例を超え史上2番目の規模となり、ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへも感染が波及しており、IHR基準の全てに該当する重大な国際的公衆衛生事象である。
triage.notes: ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、スイスへの感染拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが流行の震源地であり主題国。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola Cases Surpass 10,000 as Fears Grow Of Wider African Spread
article.articleSummary: On Oct 27, 2026, Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, surpasses 10,000 confirmed cases with 10,060 cases and 4,887 deaths per the public health institute. This marks the largest and deadliest Congo outbreak to date, the second-largest and second-deadliest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Kenya reported its first case this month, totaling nine cases after a Congo-traveled man died in Nairobi; Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case last week. Uganda had 20 cases in May–June and was declared Ebola-free by WHO in August; Ugandan officials say there are no current cases and plan 21-day quarantines for returning travelers with Congo exposure. An imported/exported case involves the wife of a Swiss diplomat, believed by Switzerland to have contracted it in Uganda; she and her husband were flown to Switzerland for treatment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱症例が1万人を突破、アフリカ全体への拡大懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最大規模のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（1万人超の感染、死者4,887人）が発生し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの国際的な感染拡大が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスへの感染拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主たる発生国であるDRCのみを記載。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola poza granicami DR Konga. Rośnie niepokój w Afryce i Europie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola beyond the borders of the DRC. Concern grows in Africa and Europe.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak spreading beyond the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) with more than 10,000 infections and 4,887 deaths reported in the DRC. The virus has reached Uganda (20 infections, 2 deaths); despite a WHO-affirmed Ebola-free status in August, Kampala maintains precautions and travelers returning from the DRC face a 21-day quarantine. Kenya reported its October case, a man traveling from the DRC via Uganda who died in Nairobi; eight more infections followed. Nigeria became the fourth African country to detect Ebola. An infection was confirmed in the wife of a Swiss diplomat; she did not travel to the DRC, with Swiss authorities saying exposure may have occurred in Uganda. The diplomat and his wife were treated in Switzerland. The WHO deems May outbreak the largest in the DRC, though it is smaller than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone) with over 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国国境を越えるエボラ出血熱。アフリカとヨーロッパで懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で1万人超の感染・約4,887人の死亡が報告され、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへと感染が拡大しており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性、異常性、国際拡大、渡航制限）に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ発生を主題とし、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの拡大を報告しているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Alertan en Brasil sobre vacunación incompleta contra el dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil Warns About Incomplete Dengue Vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Brazil reports that over three million adolescents have received the first dose of Takeda's dengue vaccine, with nearly four million doses distributed but not yet administered. In total, more than 11.8 million dengue vaccine doses have been supplied, including 7.6 million first doses and 4.2 million second doses. The immunogen, Qdenga, requires two doses spaced three months apart. The immunization campaign under Brazil’s Unified Health System began in the most affected municipalities and has expanded nationwide for children and adolescents aged 10–14. Eder Gatti, director of the National Immunization Program, emphasized accelerating coverage before the Southern Hemisphere summer, noting that El Niño could intensify dengue transmission. The supply for the eligible population is guaranteed. The Takeda contract covers nine million doses in 2026 and the same in 2027, though production limits prevent immediate universal coverage.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル、デング熱ワクチン接種の未完了について警鐘

article.articleHeadline: WHO urges Zimbabwe to assess Ebola preparedness amid regional spread
article.articleSummary: Zimbabwe is urged by the WHO to assess Ebola preparedness and bolster surveillance as the outbreak spreads across Africa. In Harare on Oct 26, the WHO Representative Desta Tiruneh announced two grants totaling 16.82 million USD to strengthen Zimbabwe's pandemic readiness. Although Zimbabwe has not reported Ebola cases, authorities should implement fully functional surveillance systems, points of entry screening, laboratory diagnostic capacity, and rapid response teams to contain any imported cases. With Ebola's spread from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya and Nigeria, cross-border transmission remains a real threat. Tiruneh called for reviewing national response plans, closing operational gaps, and reinforcing coordination across administrative levels for rapid detection. The current DRC outbreak is described as the largest and deadliest yet, the second-largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa.

article.articleHeadline: Jedan zdravstveni radnik ubijen, drugi ranjen u napadu u Kongu zbog epidemije ebole
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: One healthcare worker killed, another injured in an attack in Congo over the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: In Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak has reached nearly 10,000 confirmed cases with about a 48.6% case fatality rate. As of Friday, 9,964 cases were reported, with totals exceeding 10,000 and roughly half of infections resulting in death. An attack in Bafvasende killed a veteran hospital technician and injured a colleague during community outreach to raise awareness, after locals accused responders of contaminating water. Declared in May, this is described as the fastest-spreading, most lethal Ebola outbreak in Congo’s history, spanning 66 health zones across eight provinces. Cases have appeared in five countries, including Uganda and France (no active cases there) and Kenya and Nigeria. About 80% of new infections involve people not under surveillance, indicating undetected transmission chains. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo ebolavirus.

The crisis has crossed borders, with Kenya reporting nine cases (including a Nairobi death tied to travel from DRC), Nigeria becoming Africa’s fourth country affected, and Uganda reporting 20 May–June cases largely imported from DRC. WHO had declared Uganda Ebola-free in August, but authorities have tightened measures, including a 21-day quarantine for returnees from DRC to curb reintroduction. The outbreak’s cross-border spread raises concern for additional African nations despite ongoing containment efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Pemerintah Aktifkan SIZE untuk Deteksi Dini Penyakit Zoonosis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Government Activates SIZE for Early Detection of Zoonotic Diseases
article.articleSummary: On 27 October 2026, Indonesia activates the first phase of the Zoonosis and Emerging Infectious Diseases Information System (SIZE) in Java–Bali to enable early detection of zoonotic and emerging infections. SIZE links human, animal, and environmental health data across the Ministries of Health, Agriculture, and Environment to speed outbreak tracing and reduce economic impact. The initial activation covers 40 regencies/cities in Java–Bali, chosen for zoonosis endemism and high population density (about 60% of Indonesians) plus infrastructure readiness. The mobility of people and livestock, including cattle shipments Bali–Java, raises cross-border transmission risk; example threats include anthrax if infected meat is consumed. Nipah, hantavirus, and rabies are highlighted as pathogens needing vigilance. Yogyakarta Special Region (DIY) remains rabies-free but continues surveillance of dog and other animal bites. SIZE aims to unify reporting from Puskesmas and veterinary services (Puskeswan) to trace sources and coordinate prevention and response.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola fever outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed the lives of more than 5,000 people.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 27, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 10,060 Ebola virus disease cases with more than 5,000 deaths, according to the Ministry of Health and Associated Press reporting. The outbreak, declared May 15 in the DRC, is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rarer strain, and is the deadliest in the country’s history, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak. The virus has spread to 66 health zones across eight provinces, expanding from three initial foci. Hospitals are severely overwhelmed, with critical bed shortages and health workers striking over delayed salaries. Cases of Ebola have also been confirmed in neighboring Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, underscoring cross-border transmission and the need for regional coordination and the continued implementation of public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Beni : 13 nouveaux guéris quittent les centres de traitement en pleine expansion de l'épidémie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Beni: 13 new recoveries leave treatment centers as the outbreak expands.
article.articleSummary: Thirteen Ebola patients were discharged from treatment centers in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu, on October 27, 2026, after about ten days of care; their final tests were negative. Among them is Tsongo Sivasimire, a nurse infected while treating a patient; he spent 14 days in care and noted initial symptoms of anorexia, headaches and severe fatigue. He urged the public to support response teams to break transmission chains. Dr. Jérémie Muhindo, head of care, said these recoveries show Ebola can be cured and urged early hospital care and reduced stigma toward survivors. In North Kivu, 58 new cases were reported in 24 hours, while Ituri remains the epicenter with over 7,200 cumulative cases; North Kivu now accounts for most new infections. The case-fatality rate stands at 56% per the latest INS report, and authorities say the outbreak may be shifting its active epicenter toward North Kivu.

article.articleHeadline: As Ebola Spreads to Multiple Countries, the Importance of NV-387 Oral Gummies Treatment Cannot be Understated - Phase II Clinical Trial Advancing Towards the Second Part, Says NanoViricides
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths, the fastest-growing Ebola event to date. The virus has spread to Kenya and Nigeria; a DRC traveler’s movement to Uganda previously sparked a small outbreak, and a Kenyan death led to at least eight secondary cases with about 134 contacts traced. Tumaini vaccine trials include Ervebo (not BDBV-specific), ChAdOx1-BDBV, and Moderna BDBV-mRNA in a ring-vaccination framework; concerns cite potential escape mutants and antibody-dependent enhancement. No approved vaccine or treatment exists for Ebola BDBV; NV-387 Oral Gummies is the only oral drug in Phase II trials in the DRC, with Phase IIA enrollment of about 20 patients and a 28-day survival endpoint, likely advancing to Phase IIB. The PARTNERS trial of antibody cocktails and remdesivir has enrolled 350+ participants since July 2, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Mais de 3 milhões de adolescentes precisam da 2ª dose contra dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 3 million adolescents need a second dose of the dengue vaccine.
article.articleSummary: More than 3 million Brazilian adolescents aged 10–14 still need the second dengue vaccine dose, given three months after the first for full protection. Brazil's National Immunization Program reports over 11.8 million doses administered nationwide—7.6 million first doses and 4.2 million second doses. About 4 million doses distributed to municipalities remain unused. Dengue typically rises in summer and may intensify this season due to the El Niño phenomenon. Vaccination began in the most affected municipalities and has since expanded nationwide. The campaign targets 10–14-year-olds. A contract with a Japanese manufacturer producing Qdenga provides 9 million doses in 2026 and 9 million more in 2027 to sustain the program.
