article.articleHeadline: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو يثير مخاوف وصعوبة في الاستجابة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo raises concerns and difficulties in responding.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a major concern; the WHO warns that despite some positive signals, international support is essential amid funding cuts over the past 18 months. Speaking at the 76th WHO Regional Committee for Europe in Copenhagen (27-29 October 2026), Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus cited ongoing response difficulties. He also noted a hantavirus outbreak linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius, with the United Kingdom reporting cases, Switzerland sequencing the genome, Spain arranging Tenerife disembarkations with EU backing, and the Netherlands caring for crew; Spain's health minister Monica Garcia was thanked. The briefing warns of financial hardship from catastrophic health costs, rising non-communicable diseases, mental-health issues, and health-worker strain, along with measles reemergence in some previously eliminated countries. Climate change, violence against women, and conflicts such as Ukraine's war remain threats, and WHO continues one of its most complex emergency responses in Ukraine.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱流行が懸念と対応の困難さを引き起こす
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱流行についてWHO事務局長が国際的な資金不足と対応の困難さを公に警告しており、WPRO基準の重症度・流行継続性・管理可能性(国際支援要請)が複数該当し、社会的・政治的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事はWHO欧州地域委員会でのTedros事務局長の発言内容を伝えるもので、DRCのエボラ流行が主題。ハンタウイルス(クルーズ船関連、英国・スイス・スペイン・オランダ)や麻疹再興、ウクライナ情勢は対象国リスト外または副次的言及のため除外。資金不足による対応困難が強調されている点が特記事項。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية: حالات الإصابة بفيروس "إيبولا" في البلاد تجاوزت 10 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola virus infections in the country have surpassed 10,000.
article.articleSummary: As of Tuesday, October 27, 2026, confirmed Ebola virus infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 10,000, reaching 10,060 cases according to a government release. The latest report from the DRC Public Health Institute documents the current total of confirmed infections, with no accompanying figures for deaths provided. The figure highlights the ongoing burden of Ebola within the country, underscoring continued transmission and the need for ongoing surveillance and public health response. The article does not specify geographic hotspots, the outbreak timeline, or the methods used to confirm infection, nor does it mention infection sources or any imported/exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:国内のエボラウイルス感染者数が1万人を突破
triage.triage_reason: エボラ確定症例が1万人を超えるという重大な公衆衛生上の事態であり、致死率の高い疾患の大規模流行はIHR基準およびWPRO基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 死亡者数、地理的ホットスポット、流行の時系列、感染確認方法、感染源、輸入/輸出症例の有無について記事内に情報なし。継続的な感染拡大が示唆されており、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : 25 Cholera Patients From Zambia Railways Passenger Train Evacuated To Chilanga Urban Clinic
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak prompts evacuation in Zambia: 25 cholera patients were evacuated from a Zambia Railways passenger train to Chilanga Urban Clinic, while the train en route to Livingstone was intercepted in the Mapepe-Kachenjela area of Chilanga District following an outbreak notification. The Ministry of Health reports 475 other passengers on board were vaccinated to contain the situation. One passenger who boarded at Kapiri Mposhi developed cholera symptoms on the train, triggering an alert and on-board assessment. The train has been fumigated and is expected to resume to Livingstone once the last passenger is vaccinated. The government will erect resting tents to provide temporary shelter; affected passengers will receive clean, treated drinking water and meals. MOH is coordinating with Livingstone staff to monitor for new symptoms for a rapid response.

triage.headline_ja: ザンビア：ザンビア鉄道旅客列車のコレラ患者25名、チランガ都市クリニックへ搬送
triage.triage_reason: コレラ感染者が鉄道旅客から発生し、475名への緊急ワクチン接種や列車の消毒・隔離など政府の積極的対応が報じられており、水系感染症としての拡大リスクと社会的関心が認められる。
triage.notes: 死亡者数や重症度の詳細、既存のザンビア国内コレラ流行状況との関連は記事から不明。今後の症例動向と保健省の対応状況を継続的に注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Angola: Moxico Leste analyse la situation de la variole dans une session ordinaire
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Angola: East Moxico analyzes the smallpox situation in an ordinary session.
article.articleSummary: Smallpox (variola) outbreak in Angola’s East Moxico Province (Leste) is under monitoring. First cases were detected in June 2025. As of 27 October 2026, about 215 patients have recovered, with 13 currently under medical follow‑up in health centers in Cazombo, Luau, and Luacano. The third ordinary session, led by Governor Crispiniano dos Santos, evaluated the outbreak and epidemiological measures to curb transmission, alongside disaster response after recent storms that destroyed 350 homes (60 razed) and left over 1,000 people in precarious conditions. East Moxico, created in 2025 to bring services closer to residents, has more than 400,000 inhabitants; its capital is Cazombo. The province borders Lunda Sul to the north, Moxico to the west and south, and the DRC and Zambia to the east; it comprises nine municipalities including Cazombo, Luacano, and Luau. No laboratory confirmation or transmission source details are provided.

triage.headline_ja: アンゴラ：東モシコ州が通常会合で天然痘の状況を分析
triage.triage_reason: 天然痘（variola）は1980年に根絶宣言された疾患であり、真正な症例であればIHR上自動的にPHEIC相当となるため、検査確認が得られていない点を含めて直ちにフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルである。
triage.notes: 記事の発生地はアンゴラ東モシコ州であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空とした。DRC・ザンビアは国境を接する地理的言及のみで、当該国での発生を示すものではない。また『天然痘（variola）』との表記だが検査確認やヒト-ヒト感染源の詳細がなく、致死例の報告もないため、実際にはサル痘（mpox）等の誤訳・誤認の可能性もあり、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: SP registra casos de hantavirose; saiba os sintomas e como se proteger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: São Paulo records cases of hantavirus disease; learn the symptoms and how to protect yourself.
article.articleSummary: São Paulo reports four cases of Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS) and one death in 2026, with authorities warning of the disease's severity. Since 2007, the state has recorded 199 HCPS cases and 101 deaths, a case fatality of about 51%. Transmission is zoonotic from wild rodents, via inhalation of aerosols containing urine, feces, or saliva; contact with contaminated secretions can also transmit infection. Early symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, abdominal discomfort, nausea, and vomiting; progression may lead to cough, rapid breathing, hypotension, tachycardia, and severe dyspnea. Diagnosis relies on serology in reference public laboratories; there is no specific antiviral treatment, with care focused on symptom control and organ support. Prevention emphasizes reducing rodent contact, ventilating closed spaces, damp cleaning (not dry sweeping), and using gloves and appropriate masks; store food securely and seal entry points. Prompt recognition and reporting to surveillance support case investigation and control.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロ州でハンタウイルス症候群の症例を記録；症状と予防法について
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いハンタウイルス肺症候群だが、齧歯類からの人獣共通感染でヒト-ヒト感染はなく、2007年以降継続する既知の地域流行パターンであるため、国際的拡大リスクは低い。ただし重症度が高いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 2026年にサンパウロ州で4症例・1死亡が報告されたが、2007年以降の累計199症例・101死亡（致死率約51%）という既知の地域流行パターンの一部。齧歯類由来の人獣共通感染症でヒト-ヒト感染はなく、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威とはみなされない。地方の健康啓発記事的な性質が強い。

article.articleHeadline: صحيفة عمون : رقم قياسي لإصابات إيبولا في الكونغو .. ومخاوف من تمدد التفشي
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ammon Newspaper: A record number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and fears of the outbreak spreading.
article.articleSummary: Record Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed infections, totaling 10,060, with 4,887 deaths. The surge, beginning mid-May, is attributed to the rare Bundibugyo strain and marks the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC, and the second-largest ever globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (over 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone). Fears of regional spread persist: Kenya reported its first case in October, with nine cases total after a Nairobi death linked to travel from Congo via Uganda. Nigeria confirmed a case, becoming the fourth African country to report Ebola. Uganda recorded 20 cases in May–June (mostly arrivals from Congo); the WHO declared Uganda virus-free in August. Ongoing concerns about further cross-border transmission remain.

triage.headline_ja: アモン紙：コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染者数が記録的水準に達し、流行拡大への懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで記録的規模（1万人超の感染、死者4,887人）のエボラ流行が発生し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの越境伝播も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: 記事ではケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・シエラレオネ・リベリアへの言及があるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外した。DRCが主題の発生地域として該当。

article.articleHeadline: Africa Ebola Outbreak Passes 10,000 Cases, Mostly In DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Africa surpasses 10,000 confirmed cases, with 10,060 infections and 4,887 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo since May, the vast majority of the tally. Cases have also appeared in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda amid a Bundibugyo-species outbreak spanning east, west and central Africa. Uganda, which had 20 cases and 2 deaths and was declared Ebola-free by the WHO in late August, remains in focus; Kenya reports two deaths after confirming its first case on Oct 6. Nigeria reports a single confirmed case—a Swiss woman who contracted the virus after a trip to Uganda and was evacuated to Switzerland; 53 contacts have been identified. The patient developed symptoms on Oct 7, sought care in Abuja on Oct 11, and tested positive on Oct 20. No approved vaccines or treatments exist for Bundibugyo Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカのエボラ出血熱流行、症例数が1万人を突破 ― 大半がコンゴ民主共和国
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国を中心に1万人超の症例・4887人の死亡が報告され、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ、さらにはスイスへも拡大しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大イベント。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・スイスでの症例も報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ブンディブギョ種には承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya, Ebola: venti persone escono dalla quarantena, ma l'emergenza non è finita
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya, Ebola: Twenty people leave quarantine, but the outbreak is not over.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (a form of Ebola) outbreak in Kenya remains active as 20 people were released from quarantine after 21 days of symptom-free observation on Oct 26; 98 contacts continue to be monitored. WHO data up to Oct 26 show Kenya with 9 confirmed cases and 2 deaths; eight additional infections occurred among people already under surveillance, with no documented uncontrolled community transmission. The first Kenyan case was linked to travel from the Democratic Republic of the Congo via Uganda; Nigeria also reported an imported case. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, by Oct 20, over 9,700 confirmed cases and about 4,600 deaths reflect a substantially larger crisis. No vaccines or specific treatments exist; key measures are rapid case identification, supportive clinical care, protection of health workers, and meticulous contact tracing. Stigma and mistrust can hinder surveillance, highlighting the need for community engagement and cross-border coordination.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、エボラ出血熱：20人が隔離を解除されたが、緊急事態は終わっていない
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準のうち深刻性・異常性・国際拡大の3基準に該当し、DRCでは9700例超・4600人死亡という大規模流行が継続、複数国への越境拡大も確認されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアにおけるエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行だが、ケニアはトリアージ対象国リストに含まれないため除外。一方、DRCは9700例超・4600人死亡という大規模流行の発生源国として記事内で具体的に言及されており、対象国リストに含まれるためverified_locationsに含めた。ウガンダ・ナイジェリアも輸入例として言及されているが対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: Уже эпидемия! В Конго бушует крупнейшая в истории страны вспышка Эболы - более 10 000 заболевших
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Already an epidemic! In the Congo, the largest Ebola outbreak in the country's history is raging - more than 10,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) surpasses 10,000 confirmed cases (10,060) with nearly 50% fatalities, the deadliest and fastest-spreading outbreak in the country’s history. The May-declared epidemic is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, initially undetectable by standard tests, suggesting many infections went unrecorded as transmission continued for months before detection. Response is hampered by armed conflict, poor roads, distrust and misinformation, violence against health workers, and payroll-driven strikes. Relative to the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, this event has at least triple the cases and deaths and spans three regions; cases have also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria. In total, infections have been identified in five countries, including Uganda and France, where there are currently no active cases. About 80% of registered cases are not linked to known contacts, indicating ongoing transmission chains, and at least half of deaths occur outside hospitals. The outbreak overloads Congo’s health system, disrupts other vaccination programs (including cholera), and reduces school attendance.

triage.headline_ja: もはや感染症流行！コンゴで史上最大のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが猛威を振るう - 感染者1万人超
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最大規模（1万人超、致死率約50%）のエボラ出血熱流行が発生し、複数国への拡散も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の多くに該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、フランスへの感染拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。標準検査で検出困難なBundibugyoエボラウイルスが原因であり、長期間未検出のまま感染が拡大した可能性が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: plus de 10.000 cas désormais recensés en Afrique
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: More than 10,000 cases now recorded in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola, transmitted by contact with bodily fluids, causes severe hemorrhagic fever and has resulted in 10,060 infections and 4,887 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of 27 October 2026, with around 2,684 recoveries and a case-fatality rate near 50%. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus and was declared on 15 May, making it the worst in the DRC since 2018–2020 (about 2,300 deaths and 3,500 cases). Cross-border spread has occurred: 20 cases and 2 deaths in Uganda; 9 cases and 2 deaths in Kenya; and an imported case in Nigeria—the patient, a 42-year-old Swiss woman married to Swiss embassy staff in Abuja, who had traveled via Uganda. Response is hampered by limited resources in areas with armed groups; distrust has led to attacks on health workers, including a nurse killed in Tshopo. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, though Ervebo doses have been given in DRC as part of a clinical trial.

article.articleHeadline: Guia completo aponta doze sinais de leptospirose e indica tratamento
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Comprehensive guide identifies twelve signs of leptospirosis and recommends treatment.
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis, a zoonotic bacterial infection, is transmitted mainly via the urine of infected animals, notably rats, with risk elevated during heavy rains and floods. Early signs include high fever, severe headache, malaise, and chills, plus myalgias (calves, back, abdomen) and gastrointestinal symptoms. Dermatologic and ocular signs (conjunctival injection) may appear; progression can lead to Weil disease with jaundice, renal failure, and pulmonary hemorrhage. Diagnosis relies on clinician assessment and laboratory tests for Leptospira antibodies or the organism, supported by CBC, chest radiography, and ECG. Treatment depends on disease stage: antibiotics for early/moderate cases, analgesics and antipyretics, and rigorous hydration; severe renal involvement may require peritoneal dialysis. No location-specific outbreaks are stated.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Cases in DR Congo Surpass 10,000 in Fastest-Growing Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases with 4,887 deaths, marking the fastest-growing and deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. Declared May 15, the outbreak has spread across 66 health zones in eight provinces and crossed into neighboring East and Central Africa. About 80% of new cases occur outside monitored transmission chains, straining surveillance and health systems amid public mistrust. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain with no vaccine or approved treatment. The World Health Organization announced the first vaccine clinical trial has been rolled out. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention notes that controlling the outbreak will require at least 95% of cases to come from known contacts. Containment remains precarious due to healthcare shortages and cross-border transmission.

The information highlights a substantial, widening Ebola outbreak in Africa, underscoring ongoing public health risk and the need for continued surveillance and response across affected nations.

article.articleHeadline: ಕಾಂಗೊದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಬೋಲಾ ಅಟ್ಟಹಾಸ: 10 ಸಾವಿರಕ್ಕೂ ಅಧಿಕ ಮಂದಿಗೆ ಸೋಂಕು ದೃಢ | Ebola ravages Congo: Infection confirmed in over 10,000 people

article.articleHeadline: São Paulo registra quatro casos de hantavirose em 2026: conheça o quadro
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: São Paulo reports four hantavirus disease cases in 2026: learn about the clinical presentation.
article.articleSummary: São Paulo State Health Secretariat (SES-SP) warned of hantavirus’ high lethality in the state on 26 October 2026. Through September 2026, four hantavirus cases were confirmed in the region, with one death; since 2007 São Paulo has 199 diagnoses and 101 deaths (case fatality ≈51%). Brazil’s national fatality rate averages about 46.5%. SES-SP stressed early identification of suspected cases and rapid epidemiological investigation. Hantavirus is a zoonosis transmitted mainly by inhalation of aerosols from urine, feces, or saliva of wild rodents; reservoirs include the rice rat (Oligoryzomys) and Necromys species. Symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, abdominal pain, and nausea; severe cases may progress to dyspnea and renal failure (Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome). Diagnosis relies on serology in reference labs. Transmission can occur via skin breaks or mucous contact; rare person-to-person spread described with Andes virus. In Brazil, 16 of 27 states have reported SCPH cases, including São Paulo; the HV Hondius cruise outbreak (April 2026) linked to Andes virus caused three deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Brote de Ébola en el Congo supera los 10 mil casos y casi 5 mil muertes: ¿Ya hay vacunas?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 10,000 cases and nearly 5,000 deaths: Are there vaccines yet?
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths (case fatality ~48.6%), with data through Oct 25, 2026. Declared May 15, the epidemic is the second deadliest and most contagious since West Africa 2014–2016. Recovered: 2,684; contact tracing: 81.6%. The outbreak spans 66 health zones in eight provinces, led by Ituri and North Kivu with 32 and 58 new cases. Also affected: Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, South Kivu, and Ubangi. Hotspots include Beni (35), Mandima (11), Bunia (8). Cross-border spread includes Uganda: 20 cases, 2 deaths (15 imported); Kenya: 9 cases, 2 deaths; Nigeria: 1; France: 1, a returned doctor; no active cases. Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatment; two vaccines are in Phase 1. Congo began using Ervebo (Zaire strain) with cross-protection signals in animals; WHO is evaluating others.

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria.- El ECDC envía a un equipo de expertos a Nigeria para...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nigeria - The ECDC sends a team of experts to Nigeria to ....
article.articleSummary: ECDC has dispatched a team of experts to Nigeria to reinforce investigations and local response to Ebola after a case was detected in Nigeria and nine confirmed in Kenya, amid the Bundibugyo outbreak affecting the Democratic Republic of Congo. Led by the ECDC's chief epidemiological intelligence expert, the team will advise the EU Delegation in Abuja and assist Nigerian authorities in surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and emergency preparedness and response. Since May, ECDC has supported outbreak actions, including evaluating airport exit controls in DRC and Uganda and deploying experts in South Sudan. Deployments are coordinated by the EU Health Security Working Group, with collaboration from Africa CDC, the European Commission, WHO, the EU Delegation in Nigeria, and Nigeria CDC. Risk to Europeans is low if precautions are followed; very low for Europe/EEA. The EU provides preparedness checklists and post-flight risk guidance.

article.articleSummary: ECDC to send expert team to Nigeria as Ebola spreads from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to other African countries. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control will deploy experts to Abuja to support the EU delegation, aiding surveillance, contact tracing, and infection prevention and control. Since the outbreak began in May, the ECDC has coordinated with the EU Health Working Group and WHO. The latest risk assessment finds the probability of infection for Europeans in affected areas in Kenya and Nigeria to be low if precautions are followed, and the risk to Europe is low. article.articleHeadline: Nigéria: centro europeu de doenças envia peritos após 10 mil casos de Ébola no Congo

article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, now surpassing 10,000 cases, continues spreading in Africa with Kenya and Nigeria reporting cases. Nigeria is the fourth African country to report an Ebola case in this outbreak. Kenya reported its first Ebola case on Oct 6; eight contacts of confirmed cases developed symptoms and tested positive after laboratory analyses, and the UN said they were immediately transferred to the Ebola treatment center in Nairobi; 20 more contacts were released from quarantine. ECDC assessment: very low risk for Europeans; low risk for people living or traveling to affected areas in Kenya and Nigeria.

Kenya reported its first Ebola infection on October 6; by Monday eight contacts had developed symptoms and tested positive in Nairobi, while a further 20 contacts were released from quarantine. The ECDC’s latest risk assessment places Europe’s importation risk as very low and low risk for travelers to Kenya and Nigeria.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Africa exceed 10,000, most of them in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola cases in Africa exceed 10,000, with the majority in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Congolese health authorities report 10,060 confirmed infections and 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was first detected in May, the deadliest wave on record for the country. Cases have also been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. Kenya has two Ebola deaths but no confirmed infections as of Oct 6; Uganda had previously recorded 20 cases with two deaths and was declared Ebola-free by WHO in late August. Nigeria has one confirmed case, a Swiss national who contracted the virus during a trip to Uganda with her husband; authorities identified 53 contacts to curb spread. The Nigerian case is linked to Bundibugyo Ebola virus, a rare strain with no licensed vaccines or treatments. WHO cautions that containment will be complex as the outbreak extends across East, West, and Central Africa.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, Ebola surpasses 10,000 cases and nearly 5,000 deaths: four out of five infections evade the controls.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 October 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths (Bundibugyo), with no approved vaccines. Approximately 80% of new infections occur outside monitored transmission chains. The outbreak started in Ituri on 15 May and has spread to 66 health zones in eight provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu hardest hit. Healthcare capacity is strained; many deaths occur at home. Nigeria reports a single case: a 42-year-old Ugandan-born Nigerian wife of a Swiss embassy employee, who tested positive 20 October and was evacuated to Geneva; Uganda has imposed a 21-day quarantine for arrivals from Congo. Kenya has 9 cases and 2 deaths, linked to a man from Entebbe; 20 October contacts left quarantine, 98 remain. A Tumaini trial began 23 October in Bunia, using Ervebo; two Bundibugyo-targeted vaccines could enter in November. Four in five infections evade tracing.

article.articleHeadline: El ébola superó los 10.000 casos en el Congo y ya dejó casi 4.900 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpassed 10,000 cases in the Congo and has already claimed nearly 4,900 lives.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, declared May 15, has surpassed 10,000 confirmed infections and approached 5,000 deaths, with 10,060 cases and 4,887 fatalities through October 25. Case fatality rate 48.6%; 2,684 recoveries; contact tracing follow-up 81.6%. Ituri province remains the epicenter, accounting for 71.7% of confirmed cases, with spread to 66 health zones across 8 of the country’s 26 provinces. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus variant; unlike the Zaire strain, there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this variant. International spread includes cases in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, with France reporting an imported case, heightening cross-border concerns. This is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's history and ranks as the world’s second-largest Ebola outbreak after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic.

article.articleHeadline: Raj puts Ebola watch on flyers from high-risk nations
article.articleSummary: Rajasthan, India, tightens Ebola surveillance with a 21-day protocol for international travellers from Ebola-affected nations amid Bundibugyo virus disease activity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and parts of Africa. Travelers from DR Congo, Uganda, Nigeria and Kenya will be screened at Jaipur airport, with tracing if entering from other Indian cities. The 21-day monitoring window aligns with Ebola’s maximum incubation period; suspected cases will be isolated in designated facilities, and quarantine arrangements are being prepared in Jaipur and other cities to ensure rapid response. Health teams will verify recent travel histories, focusing on symptomatic individuals or exposure history, with coordination among airports, immigration and district health authorities. No Ebola case has been reported in Rajasthan; measures are preventive and in line with health guidance following a ministry video conference.

article.articleHeadline: เตือนภัย! สุ่มตรวจเห็ดเข็มทองกทม.เจอเชื้อปนเปื้อน
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Warning! Random checks of Bangkok enoki mushrooms found microbial contamination.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-27, Thai authorities reported random checks of enoki mushrooms sold in Bangkok markets found Listeria monocytogenes in all five samples from five shops. The samples included both domestically produced mushrooms and imports from China; the findings do not prove that all Chinese-origin enoki mushrooms in Bangkok are contaminated. Listeria is an environmental bacterium that can grow at refrigerator temperatures, so chilling does not guarantee safety. Infections can cause fever, headache, muscle pain, diarrhea or vomiting; high‑risk groups include the elderly, immunocompromised, and pregnant women, with possible septicemia, meningitis, miscarriage, or preterm birth. For mushroom lovers, wash and cook thoroughly; avoid raw consumption or relying on chilling. Monitor official announcements for product origins, specific lots, and recall actions.

triage.headline_ja: 警告！バンコクのエノキタケ抜き取り検査で菌汚染を検出
triage.triage_reason: バンコク市場のエノキタケ全検体からリステリア菌が検出されたが、現時点でヒトの感染症例は報告されておらず、情報が限定的なため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 中国産エノキタケも検体に含まれていたが、汚染が確認されたのはバンコク市場での販売品であり、発生地はタイ。中国は輸入元として言及されているのみで、イベント発生国とは見なさない。

article.articleHeadline: WHO reports over 10,000 Bundibugyo Ebola virus cases in DRC
article.articleSummary: Over 10,000 Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease cases have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as of 2026-10-27, per the World Health Organization. More than 2,600 people have recovered. The outbreak continues, with progress cited in developing new vaccine and treatment candidates through ongoing clinical trials. Efforts to strengthen laboratory testing, treatment capacity, infection prevention and control, community engagement, and surveillance are ongoing across affected areas to interrupt transmission and save lives. WHO and the DRC government, with partners, coordinate public health interventions and sustained response activities to end the outbreak. Sustained commitment, community trust, solidarity, and safe access to affected communities are emphasized as essential to protect vulnerable populations from further infections and deaths.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、DRCでブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス症例が10,000人を超えたと報告
triage.triage_reason: 大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（10,000例超）が継続中であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: WHOが大規模症例数を報告しており、ワクチン・治療薬の臨床試験が進行中。継続的なアウトブレイクでフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola supera 10 mil casos na África, maioria na RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 10,000 cases in Africa, most in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Ebola cases in Africa exceed 10,000, with the majority in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), reporting 10,060 infections and 4,887 deaths. The DRC outbreak, the deadliest among its 17 Ebola outbreaks, was first detected in May and has spread to Nigeria and Kenya after reaching Uganda. Nigeria confirmed a single case in a Swiss woman who contracted the virus while traveling in Uganda with her husband and was evacuated to Switzerland. Kenya has reported two deaths since Oct 6. Uganda, which had 20 cases and two deaths, was declared Ebola-free by the WHO in late August. A key challenge is the Bundibugjo (Bundibugyo) strain, for which there is no vaccine or treatment. Doses of the Ervebo vaccine (effective against the Zaire strain) have begun in the DRC as part of clinical trial. The WHO warns of a more complex containment task as the virus moves westward.

triage.triage_reason: DRCを中心に複数国へ拡大し死亡者多数、国際的拡大とワクチン未対応株による制御困難性からIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: The number of cases in DR Congo has surpassed 10,000 — Fears of the epidemic spreading across Africa.

Kenya has reported two deaths, its first case recorded on Oct 6. Nigeria’s only confirmed case is a Swiss woman infected after traveling to Uganda with her husband, who was later moved to Switzerland; Nigeria identified 53 contacts. The patient showed symptoms Oct 7, sought care in Abuja Oct 11, and tested positive on Oct 20.

article.articleHeadline: Първата пациентка с ебола в Нигерия бе евакуирана в Швейцария - Новини от Dnes.bg
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The first female Ebola patient in Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland - News from Dnes.bg.
article.articleSummary: A Swiss citizen treated for Ebola in Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland with her husband for medical care. Nigeria is monitoring 52 contacts of the first confirmed Ebola case. The patient left Abuja on Monday with permission from Health Minister Muhammad Pate; her condition has improved and she is stable, though she may still be contagious. Her husband, a diplomat, is asymptomatic. They flew to Switzerland; she is treated at Geneva University Hospital, while he is isolated in Zurich. Swiss authorities say there is no risk to the public. WHO Africa Director Mohamed Janabi said Nigerian teams stabilized her after the acute phase and that there are no active cases. Contact tracing continues. The woman had returned from Uganda; she did not visit Congo. Kenya reports nine cases (two deaths); Congo has over 9,900 cases and 4,800 deaths since May; WHO warns this is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak to date.

article.articleHeadline: Congo: el ébola superó los 10.000 casos y ya dejó casi 4.900 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Ebola has surpassed 10,000 cases and has already left nearly 4,900 dead.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a variant distinct from Zaire. As of 27 October 2026, the outbreak has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases and about 4,900 deaths, with a case-fatality rate of 48.6%; 2,684 patients have recovered. Declared 15 May, it is one of the deadliest in the country’s history and the most extensive and lethal in Africa to date. Ituri province in the east is the epicenter, accounting for 71.7% of cases, with transmission across 66 health zones in 8 of 26 provinces. Cross-border spread has reached Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, and France reported an imported case. There is no approved vaccine for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, complicating control efforts. The situation underscores expanding geographic reach and the urgent need for public health measures to mitigate international spread.

article.articleHeadline: إصابات فيروس إيبولا في الكونجو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 10 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 10,000.
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, Oct 27, 2026 — Official data show Ebola virus infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeding 10,000, with 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths reported by the DRC Public Health Institute. The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, began in mid-May and has become the largest and deadliest Ebola wave in the DRC, surpassing the 2018-2020 epidemic. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record globally, after the West Africa 2014-2016 outbreak that infected more than 28,600 people and killed over 11,000, primarily in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラウイルス感染者数が1万人を超える

article.articleHeadline: Дезинформация об Эболе привела к нападению на медиков в ДР Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Disinformation about Ebola led to an attack on medical workers in DR Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, with 4,887 deaths reported by October 25, 2026. Amid the outbreak, frontline medical workers face violence rooted in misinformation. In Bafwasende, locals accused responders of contaminating a water source to spread the virus. On October 24, a crowd attacked anti-epidemic teams; a nurse was killed and the school principal was severely injured and hospitalized. The National Institute of Public Health of Congo notes that 40 of the last 46 deaths occurred in towns rather than Ebola treatment centers, signaling ongoing challenges with early detection and timely care. Authorities say disinformation about the outbreak is fueling hostility toward health workers, complicating outbreak response in affected communities.

triage.headline_ja: エボラに関する誤情報がDRコンゴで医療従事者への襲撃を引き起こす

triage.notes: 死亡者の多くが治療センター外で発生しており、早期発見・治療体制に課題。誤情報による暴力が対応の障害となっている点も重大な懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola se širi Afrikom. EU poslala epidemiološki tim u Nigeriju
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is spreading across Africa. The EU has sent an epidemiological team to Nigeria.
article.articleSummary: Ebola is spreading from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, with Nigeria confirmed as the fourth African country affected. The current outbreak, the largest in the DRC, began in May and has since crossed borders into Uganda, then Kenya and Nigeria. Kenya reported its first Ebola case on October 6; as of October 26, eight additional Kenyan contacts of the initial patient were laboratory-confirmed, underscoring ongoing transmission. All patients are being treated at the Ebola treatment center in Nairobi, and the United Nations said twenty contacts in Kenya were released from quarantine after not developing symptoms. In response, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) has dispatched teams to Nigeria to advise on surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and crisis preparation. The ECDC assesses the overall risk to Europeans as very low, and low for travelers to Kenya or Nigeria.

article.articleHeadline: Weak contact tracing persists as Ebola cases surpass 10,000 in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases (10,060) and 4,887 deaths (48.6% fatality rate) since the outbreak was declared in May. The Bundibugyo virus strain has affected eight provinces—Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, South-Ubangi and North Ubangi. Early detection and contact tracing remain weak, with only about 12% of confirmed cases identified among previously known contacts, leaving transmission chains undetected. The World Health Organization Africa region emphasizes sustained control measures, broader access to affected areas, and community outreach to end the outbreak. Of 66 health zones affected, 50 (75.8%) have reported at least one new confirmed case in the last 21 days. Africa CDC will convene a high-level virtual meeting of African Ministers of Health to coordinate response. Cases linked to Congo have been reported in Uganda, France, Kenya and Nigeria.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola / Cases exceed 10,000 in DR Congo - Fears of the epidemic spreading in Africa.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's ongoing Ebola outbreak surpasses 10,000 confirmed cases, with 10,060 infections and 4,887 deaths since May, making it the deadliest outbreak in the country's history. While the largest cluster remains in DRC, cases have been reported in Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; declared over by WHO in late August), Kenya (two deaths since Oct 6), and Nigeria (one confirmed imported case in a Swiss woman who contracted the disease in Uganda). Nigeria has traced 53 contacts to prevent further spread; the patient was diagnosed after seeking care in Abuja on Oct 11, with laboratory confirmation on Oct 20. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids; concerns persist about secondary spread, including possible export to Switzerland.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola supera los 10.000 casos en el Congo: casi 4.900 muertos y alarma por su rápida expansión
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola tops 10,000 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: nearly 4,900 dead and alarm over its rapid spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has reached 10,060 confirmed infections and 4,887 deaths as of October 27, 2026, making it the largest and deadliest Ebola event in Congo’s history and the second-largest globally by cumulative cases. The epidemic began May 15, 2026 in Ituri province and has expanded to eight provinces across 66 health zones, with Ituri remaining the main hotspot and North Kivu among affected regions. The observed case fatality is about 48.6%. Rapid spread and spread into other countries, combined with conflict, poor road networks, and limited health services, hinder case finding; about 80% of new infections were identified outside existing contact lists. There is currently no vaccine or antiviral approved for this Bundibugyo variant, underscoring the need for intensified surveillance, rapid lab confirmation, and public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Евакуираха първата пациентка с ебола от Нигерия в Швейцария
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The first female Ebola patient evacuated from Nigeria to Switzerland
article.articleSummary: First female Ebola virus disease (EVD) patient diagnosed in Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland for medical care. The patient, a Nigerian-Swiss citizen, departed Abuja on Monday morning with health minister Muhammed Paté’s permission, accompanied by her Swiss diplomat husband. Although stabilized and conscious before the flight, she remains infectious and is hospitalized at the University Hospital of Geneva; her husband is isolated in Zurich. Nigeria keeps 52 contacts under active monitoring. WHO Africa Director Mohamed Janabi notes no further cases registered in Nigeria after evacuation. Swiss authorities say the patient did not visit Congo and was likely infected during travel to Uganda. In the region, Kenya reports nine cases with two deaths; 20 have been released from quarantine, 98 remain under surveillance. Since May, Congo has reported more than 9,900 cases and over 4,800 deaths, with forecasts suggesting tolls could exceed 11,000.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases top 10,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo, as countries race to stop spread
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-27, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) caused by the Bundibugyo virus has reached 10,060 confirmed cases, with roughly half resulting in death, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in DRC history. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine or treatment. The outbreak has spread to 66 health zones across eight provinces and has reached three regions domestically, with cases in Kenya and Nigeria; Uganda has 21 cases and 3 deaths (no new cases since late June); France also diagnosed a case linked to a doctor who returned from DRC. Officials say at least 95% of recorded cases are from known contacts, but about 80% of cases occur outside monitored contacts, indicating ongoing transmission. More than 2,600 recoveries. Health systems face strikes, attacks on workers, and delays in care; cholera outbreaks and maternal care disruptions amid stretched services. A virtual African CDC/WHO summit is planned.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の症例が1万人を突破、各国は拡大阻止に向け対応を急ぐ

article.articleHeadline: Santa Catarina confirma novo foco da doença de Newcastle em Coronel Freitas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Santa Catarina confirms new Newcastle disease outbreak in Coronel Freitas.
article.articleSummary: New outbreak of Newcastle disease confirmed in Coronel Freitas, western Santa Catarina, Brazil, prompting intensified sanitary surveillance by the CDAS and Ministry of Agriculture. As of 24 October, the Emergency Operations Center for Animal Health (COES) completed the first surveillance round across the emergency area. Actions included inspections of more than 160 properties with chickens and turkeys and 317 subsistence poultry properties, with 78 samples collected for laboratory analysis. Four sanitary barriers, fixed and mobile, operate 24 hours to control vehicle movement and disinfect transport. More than 15 commercial farms in the region tested negative for Newcastle disease, allowing their birds to continue production, including slaughter. Surveillance remains active in western Santa Catarina, focusing on containment and preventing further spread of the virus.

triage.headline_ja: サンタカタリーナ州、コロネル・フレイタスでニューカッスル病の新たな発生を確認
